title: My vocation is love
hookLine: Thérèse finds her place in the Church's heart
carry: love in the heart of the church

lines: WHAT DO YOU WANT TO BE?
cards: What do you want to be? Thérèse's answer was: everything. Inside the walls of a small Carmel in Normandy, she writes that she feels drawn to every calling at once.
A warrior for the Church. A priest. An apostle traveling the world.
A teacher. A martyr. Each desire pulls in a different direction, and she can't live any of them from a convent cell.
The wanting itself, she says, becomes a kind of suffering. So she does what she did with the staircase. She opens her Bible.

teach.b: She turns to Saint Paul's first letter to the Corinthians, chapters twelve and thirteen. Paul describes the Church as one body with many members.
Some are apostles, some prophets, some teachers, and he asks whether all are apostles. Not everyone can be everything.
Thérèse reads the list, and doesn't find herself in it. She keeps reading. Paul goes on to a more excellent way, and the chapter about charity, ending, "the greatest of these is charity."

teach.h: A BODY MUST HAVE A HEART.
teach.b: If the Church is a body, she reasons, it must have a heart, and that heart burns with love. Love is what moves every other member. Without it, apostles would stop preaching and martyrs would refuse to shed their blood.
Love holds every vocation inside it. Then she writes the line in her own French: ma vocation, c'est l'amour. My vocation is love.
In the heart of the Church, her mother, she will be love. And so she'll be everything she dreamed of, without leaving the cell. Then, because this is Thérèse, she brings it down to size.
She can't do great deeds, so she'll do small ones: a smile, a kind word, a sacrifice no one sees, given like flowers scattered before a king.
That's the link to yesterday. The little way isn't small in its aim. It aims at the heart of everything, one small act at a time.

how: Catholics who love Thérèse read this passage of Story of a Soul and try to offer small, hidden acts of love in ordinary life, her way of being love in the heart of the Church.

games.q: what does “my vocation is love” mean?
o: Thérèse's plan to leave Carmel for the missions
Thérèse's vow, made as a girl, to become a nun
love, the one calling that holds every other one

games.q: my vocation is love — tap the pairs.
p: burns with love, moves the rest
love, in the heart of the Church
small acts, a smile, a kind word

s: Thérèse found her place in Paul's list of apostles and teachers
she didn't find herself in the list. she found it in charity, the heart of the body.
Thérèse felt drawn to many vocations at once
warrior, priest, apostle, teacher, martyr, all from a convent cell.
for Thérèse, love means great deeds only
she can't do great deeds, so she scatters small acts like flowers.

games.q: you're Thérèse, longing to be a priest, an apostle and a martyr all at once, and you live in a cloister. what do you do with the longing?
o: choose one and forget the rest.
find the vocation that holds them all: love, in the heart of the Church.
games.why: reading 1 Corinthians, she realizes the body has a heart burning with love that moves every member: my vocation is love.

practice: Think of the next ordinary task waiting for you, dishes, an email, a drive, a diaper, and decide to do that one thing with love, as a quiet gift to someone, without announcing it.
If you pray, offer it ahead of time, the way Thérèse offered her small acts; if you don't, just picture yourself doing it gently, fully, and well.

wordCard.voice: My vocation is love. Thérèse's discovery: in the body of the Church, she will be the heart. This week ran from Teresa's friendship prayer to John's counsels, the desert, and Thérèse's elevator and heart. Today's word.

orig.note: French, Thérèse's own words: my vocation is love.

carryVoice: Your line: love in the heart of the Church. Small in size, never small in aim. That's the week.
